prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active peptide form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange has not changed my configuration, and it has sharpened why I hold it. Every member keeps B042 as the sole part, nobody argues for waiting, and the maturity evidence is not in dispute: decades of independent confirmation, several approved agents, and large randomized trials on glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The only live question is the third name and the framing of the citation. I still think the defensible unit is the discovery of GLP-1 physiology and of the active peptide, with the therapeutic consequence stated in the citation as an outcome rather than credited through a laureate slot. Holst supplies the physiology and proglucagon processing, Drucker the receptor biology, intestinotropic actions and pharmacology, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form. A single part also avoids cutting names from either side of a pairing, which would worsen the attribution problem rather than ease it.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness remains and I do not think round 1 resolved it. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others is contested, and the supplied files do not let any of us settle it; we are all relying on recollection. If the committee concludes that the active-peptide credit cannot be defended, the configuration should move to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation that names therapy development, and I would accept that as a legitimate prize. My preferred version also leaves out the person who led the long-acting analogues, so it can be read as honouring the biology and not the drugs that reached patients. Because five of six members now propose the same trio, I want to be explicit that this convergence reflects shared reasoning and a shared gap in verification, not independent confirmation of Mojsov's claim.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Knudsen as third laureate, arguing that taking a native peptide with a half-life of minutes to a once-weekly drug is a scientific achievement in protein chemistry and pharmacology, and that it produced the outcome data that make the prize pressing.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my trio and I have weighed it again. I accept that the engineering of albumin-binding, protease-resistant analogues was not routine, and I do not treat Knudsen's claim as lesser. Where I still differ is on which step the prize should name. The discovery of what the hormone is and what it does is the step on which all later drug development depended, including Knudsen's, and Mojsov's identification of the active form belongs to that step. Your version is coherent and I could vote for it if the committee decides the prize is about the therapy. My condition for moving is concrete: if the record on the active peptide shows that Mojsov's contribution was not distinct from earlier or parallel work, I would take Knudsen as the third name, as you propose. Absent that, I would not remove a discoverer to make room for a developer.

responses.point: Sandberg says he excludes Knudsen because of the three-name cap and not because her contribution is lesser, and he wants the citation to say so openly; he also accepts either trio as legitimate and offers B033 or B049 as a distinct second part if the union fits in three people.
responses.response: I agree that the citation should not imply that development is second-tier, and I have tried to word it so that the therapies appear as what the discovery made possible. I would not go further and write a sentence in the citation about who was excluded, since Nobel citations do not do that, but the committee's own report can say plainly that the cap, not a ranking of merit, drove the allocation. On a second part, I do not think B033 or B049 is worth it. With a three-person ceiling, adding Walter, or Mori and Walter, would mean taking Mojsov or Drucker out of B042, and I judge that the loss of a well-supported GLP-1 name costs more than a second prize part gains. The strength of B033 is a reason to hold it for a later year, not to dilute this one.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius agrees on the trio but says Mojsov's priority is the main thing she would want checked before committing, and floats a two-part option of Holst and Drucker with Walter, leaving Mori out.
responses.response: I share the concern, and I think we should be honest that nobody on the committee can check it from the files we were given. I would add that the Holst, Drucker and Walter option would be a poor trade. Splitting Walter from Mori breaks the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, which is its main virtue, and it does so only to compensate for a GLP-1 trio that would then be reduced to two. I would rather keep a full-strength single part with a stated fallback to Knudsen than build a two-part prize out of two mutilated halves. On the substance of B033, I agree with your reading that the unfolded protein response is a signalling principle confirmed across species over three decades, and that a basic-science prize does not need a finished therapy. That is why it is my first alternative.

responses.point: The chair accepts that his own proposal is open to challenge if development is judged the heart of the story, names El-Manira's trio as the fallback, and flags open mechanistic and safety questions for the obesity indication.
responses.response: I agree with the fallback and with the framing of the decision as a judgement on which reasonable members differ. On the obesity questions, I think they are real but they bear on how the citation is worded more than on whether the prize is ready. Central mechanisms and long-term safety remain open for essentially every widely used drug, and the evidence here, with large randomized trials and years of post-approval use, is not thin. I would keep the citation to type 2 diabetes and obesity as demonstrated clinical outcomes and avoid claiming more about mechanism than the discovery work shows. If the chair believes the citation should be narrower, for example limited to the physiology and active peptide with only a brief reference to therapy, I could accept that wording without changing the names.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that the drug-development story is carried by the citation language and not by a laureate slot, and that a two-part prize with B033 would require trimming B042 to two names, which he does not think is worth the cost to attribution.
responses.response: I agree with both parts of this and they reinforce each other. A citation that says the discoveries enabled treatment gives the therapies their due without turning a discovery prize into a product prize. I also agree on the arithmetic of a two-part prize. Cutting B042 to two names gives up either Mojsov or Drucker, and the cut would fall on the part with the most complete evidence. Where I add a qualification is on how firm our shared position should be. Your own statement notes that Mojsov's role is described differently in different accounts, and I would not want our agreement to harden into a claim that her priority is settled. I would rather the committee record that it chose the discovery framing as a judgement and that it would revisit the third name if verified priority evidence went against her.

uncertainties: Whether the record supports Mojsov's contribution to identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide as distinct from and not later than the Habener group's work; I rely on recollection and cannot verify it from the supplied files.
Whether the committee frames the prize around discovery of physiology and the active peptide or around therapy development, which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen.

Whether holding B033 for a later year, rather than pairing it now, is the right call; I judge so because of the three-person cap, but the case for Mori and Walter is strong and independent of this year's outcome.
Whether B049 can be defended at all while Eshhar is outside the credited names; I do not think trimming Rosenberg resolves that omission.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict affects B042, B033 or B049. I co-authored the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and have co-authors in common with Rickard Sandberg, including joint publications recorded in my profile, but none of the credited names on B042, B033 or B049 is a documented collaborator, trainee or colleague of mine. I do not infer ties from shared institutions or topics, and I propose no recusal.
